front_blocks.md: Define **spell check software**.

back_blocks.md: Spell check software is **built into many word processing applications** and compares the **words typed in a document** with **those held in its dictionary**.

cards.back_md: Spell check software is **built into many word processing applications** and compares the **words typed in a document** with **those held in its dictionary**.

front_blocks.md: What happens to a word that does not match the dictionary?

back_blocks.md: It is **flagged and highlighted** for the user to check, most commonly by being **underlined in red**.

cards.front_md: What happens to a word that does not match the dictionary?
cards.back_md: It is **flagged and highlighted** for the user to check, most commonly by being **underlined in red**.

front_blocks.md: Give two examples of correctly spelt words that may still be flagged.

back_blocks.md: **Proper nouns** and **words in other languages** are often flagged even when spelt correctly.

cards.front_md: Give two examples of correctly spelt words that may still be flagged.
cards.back_md: **Proper nouns** and **words in other languages** are often flagged even when spelt correctly.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A word flagged by a spell checker is always spelt incorrectly.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
If a word is **not in the dictionary but is spelt correctly**, it will still be flagged. Proper nouns are a common example.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A word flagged by a spell checker is always spelt incorrectly.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

If a word is **not in the dictionary but is spelt correctly**, it will still be flagged. Proper nouns are a common example.

front_blocks.md: Why would the name of a specific beach be flagged by a spell checker?

back_blocks.md: It is a **proper noun**, so it is **not in the dictionary**. It can be **added to the dictionary** so that it is not flagged if used again.

cards.front_md: Why would the name of a specific beach be flagged by a spell checker?
cards.back_md: It is a **proper noun**, so it is **not in the dictionary**. It can be **added to the dictionary** so that it is not flagged if used again.

front_blocks.md: Why should you use your own judgement with automated suggestions?

back_blocks.md: Automated suggestions **may not always be accurate or appropriate**, and the software may not recognise some **technical terms or jargon**.

cards.front_md: Why should you use your own judgement with automated suggestions?
cards.back_md: Automated suggestions **may not always be accurate or appropriate**, and the software may not recognise some **technical terms or jargon**.

front_blocks.md: What is the purpose of a validation check?

back_blocks.md: A validation check ensures data is **accurate, complete and meets specific criteria before it is processed**.

cards.front_md: What is the purpose of a validation check?
cards.back_md: A validation check ensures data is **accurate, complete and meets specific criteria before it is processed**.

front_blocks.md: What two things does a validation check help to achieve?

back_blocks.md: It helps to **minimise data entry errors** and to **maintain the integrity of the data**.

cards.front_md: What two things does a validation check help to achieve?
cards.back_md: It helps to **minimise data entry errors** and to **maintain the integrity of the data**.

front_blocks.md: Define **verification**.

back_blocks.md: Verification is a method of checking that data being **copied from one medium to another does not contain errors**.

cards.back_md: Verification is a method of checking that data being **copied from one medium to another does not contain errors**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Verification prevents all errors in data entry.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Verification **does not prevent all errors**. It **helps to reduce errors** in the data entry process.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Verification prevents all errors in data entry.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Verification **does not prevent all errors**. It **helps to reduce errors** in the data entry process.

front_blocks.md: Name the two most common verification techniques.

back_blocks.md: The two most common techniques are **visual verification** and **double data entry verification**.

cards.front_md: Name the two most common verification techniques.
cards.back_md: The two most common techniques are **visual verification** and **double data entry verification**.

front_blocks.md: Define **visual verification**.

back_blocks.md: Visual verification is a **manual method** of verifying data by **comparing the source with the entered data**.

cards.back_md: Visual verification is a **manual method** of verifying data by **comparing the source with the entered data**.

front_blocks.md: Define **double data entry verification**.

back_blocks.md: Double data entry verification is a method where **data is entered twice and then compared for inconsistencies**.

cards.back_md: Double data entry verification is a method where **data is entered twice and then compared for inconsistencies**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between verification and proofreading?

back_blocks.md: **Proofreading** is **checking the content of the data for errors**, while **verification** is **comparing the data with the original**.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between verification and proofreading?
cards.back_md: **Proofreading** is **checking the content of the data for errors**, while **verification** is **comparing the data with the original**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between verification and validation?

back_blocks.md: **Verification** ensures data has been **entered or copied correctly**, while **validation** makes sure the data is **sensible, reasonable and within acceptable boundaries**.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between verification and validation?
cards.back_md: **Verification** ensures data has been **entered or copied correctly**, while **validation** makes sure the data is **sensible, reasonable and within acceptable boundaries**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Validation checks that data is sensible, reasonable and within acceptable boundaries.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
That is **validation**. **Verification** is the separate check that data has been copied correctly from the original.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Validation checks that data is sensible, reasonable and within acceptable boundaries.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

That is **validation**. **Verification** is the separate check that data has been copied correctly from the original.

front_blocks.md: Give one reason why data is verified on entry.

back_blocks.md: To ensure that the data entered has been **copied correctly**.

cards.front_md: Give one reason why data is verified on entry.
cards.back_md: To ensure that the data entered has been **copied correctly**.

front_blocks.md: Why are both verification and validation needed?

back_blocks.md: Both are essential in maintaining **data accuracy and quality**.

cards.front_md: Why are both verification and validation needed?
cards.back_md: Both are essential in maintaining **data accuracy and quality**.
